new.title: Admire the Chagall windows of Metz Cathedral
new.desc: Saint-Étienne cathedral, known as the Lanterne du Bon Dieu, holds about 6,500 m² of stained glass from the 13th to the 20th century. Marc Chagall designed windows here from 1959, including the ambulatory ones with Moses, David and Jeremiah.
new.tip: Go in the morning or at midday when light fills the nave. Entry to the cathedral is free.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Étienne, Place de la Cathédrale, Metz

new.title: Visit the Centre Pompidou-Metz and its wooden roof
new.desc: Opened in May 2010 as the first regional branch of the Paris Centre Pompidou, the museum was designed by Shigeru Ban and Jean de Gastines. Its hexagonal laminated-wood roof with a Teflon-coated membrane rises around a 77 m central spire.
new.tip: Check the current exhibition before booking. The building is next to the station, so it combines well with the Imperial Quarter.
new.q: Centre Pompidou-Metz, 1 Parvis des Droits de l'Homme, Metz

new.title: Walk through the Porte des Allemands over the Seille
new.desc: This medieval fortified gate and bridge across the Seille dates from the 13th century, with work starting around 1220. It is named after the nearby hospital of the Teutonic Knights and has been a historic monument since 1966.
new.tip: Best seen from the riverside path in the evening. Part of the building houses exhibitions and events.
new.q: Porte des Allemands, Boulevard André Maginot, Metz

new.title: See the Temple Neuf on the Petit-Saulcy island
new.desc: This neo-Romanesque Protestant church was built between 1901 and 1904 in the German imperial period, to designs by Conrad Wahn. It stands on the Moselle at Place de la Comédie and has been a historic monument since 1930.
new.tip: Photograph it from the Moyen Pont or the opposite bank. Check opening times at the tourist office.
new.q: Temple Neuf, Place de la Comédie, Metz

new.title: Stroll under the arcades of Place Saint-Louis
new.desc: Medieval money changers, many of them Lombards, built the arcaded houses on this square along the line of the old Roman wall. The 14th to 16th century buildings now shelter cafés, shops and terraces.
new.tip: Pick a terrace under the arcades for a coffee in the afternoon. The square is livelier during markets and at Christmas.
new.q: Place Saint-Louis, Metz

new.title: Tour the Imperial Quarter and Metz railway station
new.desc: The station was built in 1904 to 1908 as a showpiece of German imperial power in the Neue Stadt district created after the walls came down. Its neo-Romanesque hall, imperial salon and Charlemagne stained glass make it one of the most striking stations in France.
new.tip: Walk from the station up Avenue Foch to see the quarter's villas. Allow an hour.
new.q: Gare de Metz-Ville, Place du Général de Gaulle, Metz

new.title: Step inside Saint-Pierre-aux-Nonnains, a very old church
new.desc: Often described as one of the oldest churches in Europe, this building near the Moselle has origins in the 4th century. It was restored in the 1970s and now hosts concerts and exhibitions.
new.tip: Check the events programme, since access depends on exhibitions. It sits next to the Arsenal concert hall.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Pierre-aux-Nonnains, 1 Rue de la Citadelle, Metz

new.title: Wander the Esplanade gardens to the Templars' Chapel
new.desc: The Esplanade garden was laid out from 1853 over seven years and overlooks the Moselle and the Plan d'eau. Nearby stands the octagonal Chapelle des Templiers, built between 1180 and 1220, the only surviving part of a Templar commandery.
new.tip: The chapel is usually closed, so admire it from outside or ask the tourist office about guided visits.
new.q: Chapelle des Templiers, 3 Avenue Ney, Metz

new.title: Explore Gallo-Roman Metz at the Musée de la Cour d'Or
new.desc: Founded in 1839, this museum links the former Petites Carmes abbey, the Chèvremont granary and the Trinitaires church. It shows Roman baths, the Mithras altar and a fine group of Flemish and Dutch paintings.
new.tip: Closed Tuesdays. Allow two hours for the archaeology and medieval rooms.
new.q: Musée de La Cour d'Or, 2 Rue du Haut Poirier, Metz

new.title: See Jean Cocteau's windows in Église Saint-Maximin
new.desc: Cocteau was commissioned in 1960 to create the stained glass of this church, in blue and green pastel tones. The motifs mix religious scenes with pagan and animist imagery.
new.tip: Open daily with free entry according to the tourist guide. Visit in bright light for the colours.
new.q: Église Saint-Maximin, Rue Mazelle, Metz

new.title: Visit the Maison de Robert Schuman at Scy-Chazelles
new.desc: The founding father of the European Union lived here from 1926 and died in the house in 1963. The visit covers his preserved home, a museum on European construction, his garden and the fortified church where he is buried.
new.tip: Combine it with the Mont Saint-Quentin walk. Guided visits of the house cost a little extra.
new.q: Maison de Robert Schuman, 8 Rue Robert Schuman, Scy-Chazelles

new.title: Taste mirabelle tart at Pâtisserie Claude Bourguignon
new.desc: This Metz patissier-chocolatier and tearoom is the address most often recommended for the Lorraine mirabelle plum tart. It also makes mirabelle macarons and ice cream.
new.tip: Order the tarte aux mirabelles in late summer when the fruit is in season. Ask for the mirabelle macarons.
new.q: Pâtisserie Claude Bourguignon, 31 Rue de la Tête d'Or, Metz

new.title: Eat a revisited quiche lorraine at Loiseau de Lorraine
new.desc: This restaurant at the foot of the cathedral belongs to the Bernard Loiseau group and serves Lorraine dishes with a modern twist. The quiche is reworked as an egg emulsion with confit pork belly.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner. Ask about the seasonal Lorraine menu.
new.q: Loiseau de Lorraine, Metz

new.title: Dine on Lorraine classics at Brasserie des Arts et Métiers
new.desc: A brasserie with a refined decor serving traditional Lorraine-flavoured cooking alongside seafood and fish. It is rated 12.5/20 by Gault&Millau and is part of the Maîtres Restaurateurs de France.
new.tip: Try the regional dishes on the set menu. Booking is wise on weekends.
new.q: Brasserie des Arts et Métiers, 2 bis Rue Gambetta, Metz

new.title: Try potée lorraine at Terroirs de Lorraine by the station
new.desc: A station brasserie built around regional menus, including a potée lorraine served in a modern espuma form. Gault&Millau lists menus in the 23 to 42 euro range.
new.tip: Handy before or after a train. Choose the regional menu.
new.q: Terroirs de Lorraine, Gare de Metz-Ville, Place du Général de Gaulle, Metz

new.title: Lunch under the arcades at L'Établi de Papy Louis
new.desc: A bistro-brasserie in a medieval arcade of Place Saint-Louis serving traditional French cooking. The terrace sits under the 14th century arches.
new.tip: Take an arcade table for lunch. Check the daily specials.
new.q: L'Établi de Papy Louis, 9 Place Saint-Louis, Metz

new.title: Have macarons and chocolate at Maison Caffet
new.desc: A chocolate shop with a first-floor tearoom on rue du Grand Cerf, where pastries from the ground floor are served. Reviewers single out its macarons.
new.tip: Go for afternoon tea upstairs. Buy chocolates to take home.
new.q: Maison Caffet, 17 Rue du Grand Cerf, Metz

new.title: Graze the stalls of the Marché couvert next to the cathedral
new.desc: Installed in an 18th century building at the foot of the cathedral, this covered market sells local cheese, charcuterie, pastries and spirits. The city bought the building in 1821 to serve as a market, and Distillerie de Mélanie has a mirabelle stall inside.
new.tip: Open every day except Sunday from about 8:00 to 18:00. Taste mirabelle eau-de-vie and buy a tart.
new.q: Marché couvert de Metz, Place de la Cathédrale, Metz

new.title: Sip craft beer at Brasserie Bon Poison
new.desc: Founded in Metz in 2015, this brewery is inspired by English pubs and brews accessible, characterful beers. It holds tastings on rue du XXe Corps Américain.
new.tip: Check the tasting calendar before going.
new.q: Brasserie Bon Poison, 13a Rue du XXe Corps Américain, Metz

new.title: Stroll or paddle at the Plan d'eau de Metz
new.desc: This 1970s lake along the Moselle offers walks, cycling, play areas, mini-golf, rowing and canoe-kayaking, plus a free electric shuttle boat in summer. Metz Plage takes over the banks each summer.
new.tip: Free access. The shuttle barge runs from May to September between the Quai des Régates and the Île du Saulcy.
new.q: Plan d'eau de Metz, Boulevard Poincaré, Metz

new.title: Glide on the Moselle aboard a solar boat
new.desc: Solis Mettensis runs short trips of about an hour on a solar-powered boat with limited capacity, some with Moselle wine tastings. La Compagnie des Bateaux de Metz also offers electric boat trips.
new.tip: Reserve ahead. Confirm the season and days with the operator, as hours change.
new.q: Quai des Régates, Plan d'eau, Metz

new.title: Join the Fêtes de la Mirabelle in late August
new.desc: Two weekends of festivities at the Esplanade and Plan d'eau celebrate the Lorraine mirabelle plum, with a village of about 100 exhibitors, concerts, a nautical parade and a queen's coronation.
new.tip: Free concerts at the Esplanade. The nautical parade is on the last Sunday at the Plan d'eau.
new.q: Esplanade, Metz

new.title: Browse the Christmas markets of Metz
new.desc: Metz's Christmas market runs from late November to 30 December. The Place Saint-Louis hosts around fifty chalets of regional crafts and Lorraine foods, with a carousel for children.
new.tip: Closed 24 and 25 December. Hours are about 11:00 to 21:00, later on weekends.
new.q: Place Saint-Louis, Metz

new.title: Hike the Mont Saint-Quentin above Metz
new.desc: A loop of about 8 km from the Scy-Chazelles esplanade climbs to the crest of Mont Saint-Quentin past the Fort Diou group, with views over Metz and the Moselle valley. A longer route links the Robert Schuman house.
new.tip: Waymarking is sparse, so follow a downloaded track. Wear good shoes after rain.
new.q: Esplanade de Scy-Chazelles, Scy-Chazelles

new.title: Browse the boutiques of rue Taison
new.desc: This quiet street in the old centre follows the line of the Roman cardo maximus and is lined with gift shops, bookshops, stationers and decor boutiques. It is a pleasant detour from rue des Clercs and Place Saint-Louis.
new.tip: Most shops close on Sunday. Pair it with a pause at a nearby pâtisserie.
new.q: Rue Taison, Metz

new.title: Explore Château de Malbrouck near the three borders
new.desc: This fortress of Meinsberg was built between 1419 and 1434 and takes its name from the Duke of Marlborough, who had his headquarters there in 1705. Restored by the Moselle department between 1991 and 1998, it hosts exhibitions and festivals.
new.tip: Check seasonal opening hours. A 14 km walking loop starts from Manderen.
new.q: Château de Malbrouck, Manderen-Ritzing

new.title: Climb to the ducal castle of Sierck-les-Bains
new.desc: Perched on a red sandstone spur above the Moselle, this castle is mentioned in 1067 and was a favourite residence of the dukes of Lorraine. Restoration began in 2008, and the terrace and towers are reached by stairs.
new.tip: A medieval festival takes place each August. Wear sturdy shoes for the stairs.
new.q: Château des ducs de Lorraine, Sierck-les-Bains

new.title: Ride the underground train at Fort de Hackenberg
new.desc: The largest Maginot Line work, built from 1929 to 1935, has about 10 km of galleries and 17 or more combat blocks. The guided visit uses the original electric train in the galleries.
new.tip: Visits are guided and last 2 to 2.5 hours. Wear warm clothes and check times on maginot-hackenberg.com.
new.q: Ouvrage du Hackenberg, Veckring

new.title: Walk the ramparts of Rodemack, the little Carcassonne of Lorraine
new.desc: This fortified village near Luxembourg keeps about 700 m of ramparts, a fortified gate and watchtowers. It has been one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France since 1987.
new.tip: Park outside the walls and walk the lanes. The medieval festival is on the last weekend of June.
new.q: Rodemack, Moselle

new.title: Tour the Citadel of Bitche and its underground galleries
new.desc: This fortress on a hill above Bitche is known for the siege of 1870 and its guided underground galleries. It has a museum of the 1870 war and a 1794 relief map.
new.tip: Reopened on 16 March 2025 with seasonal hours. A combined ticket with the Garden for Peace is offered.
new.q: Citadelle de Bitche, Rue de Bombelles, Bitche

new.title: See glassblowing at the Site Verrier de Meisenthal
new.desc: The former glassworks houses the Centre International d'Art Verrier, opened in 1992, a museum and the 3,200 m² Halle Verrière used for art and concerts. Visitors can watch glassblowers, and the site is known for Christmas baubles.
new.tip: Check demonstration times. The site was renovated by SO-IL and Freaks Architecture in 2021.
new.q: CIAV Site Verrier, Place Robert Schuman, Meisenthal

new.title: Visit the Saint-Louis crystal works and museum
new.desc: The Manufacture Saint-Louis is a living-heritage crystal maker with a museum. Guided workshop tours take in the hot-glass hall, paperweight workshop and cutting room.
new.tip: Tours Tuesday to Friday at 11:00 for individuals, by reservation only, about 1.5 hours. Not offered mid-July to mid-August.
new.q: Cristallerie Saint-Louis, Saint-Louis-lès-Bitche

new.title: Find the Winter Garden at the Sarreguemines faience museum
new.desc: The museum occupies the former home of Paul de Geiger, director of the faience works from 1871 to 1914. Its 1880 Jardin d'Hiver is clad in faience tiles and is a listed monument.
new.tip: Check hours before visiting. The museum also has a Gallo-Roman section.
new.q: Musée de la Faïence, 17 Rue Poincaré, Sarreguemines

new.title: Wander Fénétrange's collegiate church and horseshoe castle
new.desc: The village has a collegiate church of Saint-Rémy with a Romanesque tower, 15th century glass and an 18th century organ, plus a castle with a horseshoe courtyard rebuilt from 1766. The courtyard paving copies the church's rose window.
new.tip: The church is free to enter. Look for the rose motif in the castle courtyard.
new.q: Collégiale Saint-Rémy, Fénétrange

new.title: Learn the salt story at the Musée du Sel in Marsal
new.desc: Set in the Porte de France of Vauban's fortifications, this Moselle museum traces salt production from prehistory to today. It reopened with a new layout at the end of 2019.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday for most of the year. Admission is around 5 euros.
new.q: Musée départemental du Sel, Porte de France, Marsal

new.title: See Georges de La Tour in Vic-sur-Seille
new.desc: The Moselle departmental museum is in the painter's birthplace and holds Saint John the Baptist in the Desert and Profile of a Woman. Its collection covers the 17th to 21st centuries.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 18:00 according to one listing. Check before travelling.
new.q: Musée départemental Georges de La Tour, Place Jeanne d'Arc, Vic-sur-Seille

new.title: Walk beneath the Roman aqueduct arches of Jouy-aux-Arches
new.desc: Twelve arches of the Gallo-Roman aqueduct that carried water from Gorze to Metz stand in Jouy-aux-Arches. The aqueduct dates from the early 2nd century and has been protected since 1840.
new.tip: Free to see at any time. The village is on the Moselle cycle route south of Metz.
new.q: Aqueduc romain, Grande Rue, Jouy-aux-Arches

new.title: Watch boats ride the Saint-Louis-Arzviller inclined plane
new.desc: This boat lift on the Marne-Rhine canal, in operation since 1969, replaced a flight of 17 locks. It lifts boats about 44.5 m on a 41% slope and holds the Architecture contemporaine remarquable label.
new.tip: Run by the Zorn valley tourist society. Check boat-trip and viewing times.
new.q: Plan incliné de Saint-Louis-Arzviller, Saint-Louis

new.title: See Chagall's Peace stained-glass window in Sarrebourg
new.desc: Marc Chagall designed La Paix ou l'Arbre de vie for the Chapelle des Cordeliers, with studies dated 1974 and a final project in 1976. It is among his major late works in glass.
new.tip: Check chapel opening hours with the tourist office.
new.q: Chapelle des Cordeliers, Sarrebourg

new.title: Climb the old town of Thionville to the Tour aux Puces
new.desc: The Tour aux Puces is the old keep of the 11th century castle and is the oldest monument in Thionville. It houses the city museum, and the Beffroi and Saint-Maximin church stand nearby.
new.tip: Museum hours were Tuesday to Sunday 14:00 to 18:00 in one source. Beffroi climbs are guided.
new.q: Tour aux Puces, Thionville

new.title: Wander the Jardins Fruitiers de Laquenexy
new.desc: These 4-hectare fruit-tree gardens east of Metz carry the Jardin remarquable label and are divided into thematic spaces. They are owned by the Moselle department.
new.tip: Open Wednesday to Sunday; under-16s enter free. The autumn garden festival is in October.
new.q: Jardins Fruitiers de Laquenexy, 4 Rue Bourger et Perrin, Laquenexy

new.title: Explore the Maginot galleries of Simserhof
new.desc: This gros ouvrage at Siersthal near Bitche has about 5 km of galleries and is the most developed Maginot site for visitors. It is owned by the Pays de Bitche communauté de communes.
new.tip: Reception is at Le Légeret. Wear warm clothes underground.
new.q: Ouvrage Simserhof, Siersthal

new.title: Ride through the underground Citadel of Verdun
new.desc: The visit uses a cable-guided car through the galleries with augmented-reality glasses following a soldier named Jean. The galleries date from the 19th century and were used in the First World War.
new.tip: The galleries are about 8°C, so bring warm clothing. Not suitable for children under 8.
new.q: Citadelle souterraine de Verdun, Avenue du Soldat Inconnu, Verdun

new.title: Understand 1916 at the Mémorial de Verdun
new.desc: The museum opened in 1967 on the site of the former Fleury railway station and was fully renovated in 2016. More than 2,000 objects tell the war from both sides.
new.tip: Allow at least 1.5 hours. Full price listed at 14 euros.
new.q: Mémorial de Verdun, 1 Avenue du Corps Européen, Fleury-devant-Douaumont

new.title: Pay respects at the Douaumont Ossuary
new.desc: The ossuary holds the remains of about 130,000 unidentified soldiers of the 1916 battle, next to a cemetery of 16,142 graves. A tower financed by Americans is its signature feature, and Mitterrand and Kohl clasped hands here in 1984.
new.tip: Allow an hour. Dress respectfully.
new.q: Ossuaire de Douaumont, Fleury-devant-Douaumont

new.title: Go inside Fort de Douaumont
new.desc: The fort was a key position during the Battle of Verdun. The visit includes the 155 mm turret and the German cemetery where more than 600 soldiers lie.
new.tip: The interior stays cool and damp, so bring a jacket. Plan 1 to 1.5 hours.
new.q: Fort de Douaumont, Douaumont

new.title: See the Tranchée des Baïonnettes memorial
new.desc: A concrete shelter marks the trench where, by legend, soldiers of the 137th Infantry were buried with bayonets fixed in June 1916. Historians question the story, and the site is regarded as a mass grave.
new.tip: It lies close to the Douaumont necropolis. Visit with the ossuary.
new.q: Tranchée des Baïonnettes, Douaumont

new.title: Climb the American monument on the Butte de Montfaucon
new.desc: Dedicated in 1937 and designed by John Russell Pope, the monument is a Doric column topped by a statue of liberty, marking the 1918 Meuse-Argonne victory. 234 steps lead to a viewing platform.
new.tip: Check opening times with the ABMC, as it is linked to the Meuse-Argonne American Cemetery.
new.q: Montfaucon American Monument, Montfaucon-d'Argonne

new.title: Stroll the Renaissance Ville Haute of Bar-le-Duc
new.desc: The upper town is a protected Renaissance district of about 26 hectares with town houses of pale local stone, and is a Ville d'art et d'histoire. Saint-Étienne church holds Ligier Richier's Transi.
new.tip: The streets are steep and cobbled. The RenaissanceS festival is in early July.
new.q: Ville Haute, Place Saint-Pierre, Bar-le-Duc

new.title: Find Ligier Richier's Sépulcre in Saint-Mihiel
new.desc: The sculptor Ligier Richier was born in Saint-Mihiel, and his Sépulcre in the Saint-Étienne church is considered his last major work, before 1560. The town also has a Benedictine abbey founded in the 8th century.
new.tip: Visit the abbey library building of 1768 to 1775 as well.
new.q: Église Saint-Étienne, Saint-Mihiel

new.title: Walk the ramparts of the Montmédy citadel
new.desc: Begun under Charles V in 1545 and reworked by Vauban, the citadel crowns the upper town and has a ramparts circuit, a fortification museum and the Jules Bastien-Lepage museum.
new.tip: Access through the tourist office at 2 rue de l'Hôtel de Ville. Check admission details.
new.q: Citadelle de Montmédy, Montmédy

new.title: See the Gothic basilica of Avioth
new.desc: Called the Cathedral of the Fields, Notre-Dame d'Avioth dates from the 13th and 14th centuries and has been a classified monument since 1840. It holds a rare Black Madonna and became a basilica in 1993.
new.tip: Open daily with free self-guided visits. A restoration project is under way.
new.q: Basilique Notre-Dame d'Avioth, Avioth

new.title: View the Woëvre from Château de Hattonchâtel
new.desc: This Renaissance-revival château was rebuilt with funds from the American Belle Skinner after First World War destruction. It is a listed monument above Vigneulles-lès-Hattonchâtel and overlooks the plain.
new.tip: The château is now a hotel and wedding venue, so visit the village viewpoint.
new.q: Château de Hattonchâtel, Vigneulles-lès-Hattonchâtel

new.title: Buy fresh Madeleines de Commercy at Zins
new.desc: The Zins family has made all-butter madeleines in Commercy since 1951. The factory is visible through a window and the visit is free.
new.tip: Production is visible most days except Monday and Sunday morning. Check hours.
new.q: La Boîte à Madeleines Zins, ZAE La Louvière, Commercy

new.title: Taste dragées de Verdun at Maison Braquier
new.desc: The house traces back to 1783 and makes the sugar-almond dragées of Verdun using Avola almonds. Its Obus de Verdun is a chocolate shell that bursts to release sweets.
new.tip: Factory shop at 50 rue du Fort-de-Vaux, town shop at 3 rue Pasteur. Check hours.
new.q: Dragées Braquier, 50 Rue du Fort de Vaux, Verdun

new.title: Taste Bar-le-Duc redcurrant jam at Maison Dutriez
new.desc: Bar-le-Duc jam is made from redcurrants whose seeds are removed by hand with a goose quill. Maison Dutriez, founded in 1879 as À La Lorraine, is described as the sole remaining maker.
new.tip: Buy a small jar in the shop on rue de l'Étoile.
new.q: À La Lorraine Maison Dutriez, 35 Rue de l'Étoile, Bar-le-Duc

new.title: Dine on Meuse produce at Le Mess des Épicuriens
new.desc: A fine-dining restaurant on the Meuse quay in Verdun using produce from the Meuse valley and Grand Est, with sommelier wine pairings.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner.
new.q: Le Mess des Épicuriens, 22 Quai de la République, Verdun

new.title: Lunch at Le Bistro d'Élo by the Meuse
new.desc: Chef Élodie Louvet runs a lively modern bistro near the Meuse with contemporary dishes that change often. Gault&Millau reviewed it in 2026.
new.tip: Check the daily menu on the slate.
new.q: Le Bistro d'Élo, 55 Quai de Londres, Verdun

new.title: Sit on the quay at Brasserie Le Rallye
new.desc: A family-run brasserie on the pedestrian quays of Verdun since 1958, with a large terrace and about 50 indoor seats.
new.tip: Take a terrace table in summer.
new.q: Brasserie Le Rallye, 49 Quai de Londres, Verdun

new.title: Dine with a view at La Meuse Gourmande in Bar-le-Duc
new.desc: A gourmet restaurant on rue François de Guise rated 12/20 by Gault&Millau, praised for its view over the town. It is closed Monday and Tuesday.
new.tip: Ask for a window table.
new.q: La Meuse Gourmande, 1 Rue François de Guise, Bar-le-Duc

new.title: Eat Lorraine cooking at Brasserie du Casino in Sarreguemines
new.desc: The bistro sibling of the Michelin-starred Auberge Saint-Walfrid serves generous Lorraine dishes on the banks of the Sarre, with a terrace.
new.tip: Good lunch stop after the faience museum.
new.q: Brasserie du Casino, Sarreguemines

new.title: Dine at Le Strasbourg in Bitche
new.desc: Chef Lutz Janisch has cooked in Bitche for fifteen years in a Michelin-listed restaurant offering modern cuisine.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner.
new.q: Le Strasbourg, 24 Rue du Colonel Teyssier, Bitche

new.title: Dine by the Moselle at Arsène & Clara in Thionville
new.desc: A bistronomic restaurant and afternoon tearoom with a terrace on the Moselle at Place Simone Veil, with a seasonal menu.
new.tip: Take a terrace table for tea.
new.q: Arsène & Clara, 7 Place Simone Veil, Thionville

new.title: Taste mirabelle eau-de-vie at Distillerie Leisen
new.desc: This Malling distillery offers guided tours and free tastings of its prizewinning mirabelle spirits, with take-away sales.
new.tip: Check opening hours first.
new.q: Distillerie Leisen, 21 Grand Rue, Malling

new.title: Taste Moselle wine at the Domaine du Stromberg
new.desc: The 8.5 ha estate in Sierck-les-Bains, in the AOC Moselle's Sierck area, also makes mirabelle de Lorraine spirits with an alembic beside the press.
new.tip: Contact the estate before visiting.
new.q: Domaine du Stromberg, Sierck-les-Bains

new.title: Hike to the Rocher de Dabo and Chapelle Saint-Léon
new.desc: This pink sandstone outcrop of about 650 m is topped by the neo-Romanesque Saint-Léon chapel, built on the ruins of the castle destroyed in 1690. Hikers start from the Schlossberg car park.
new.tip: Platform access is regulated in winter. A restaurant stands near the chapel.
new.q: Rocher de Dabo, Dabo

new.title: Walk the Butte de Vauquois mine-war trail
new.desc: The butte was shattered by 519 mines in the First World War, with more than 17 km of tunnels. A 6 km circuit from the village takes about 2 hours.
new.tip: Underground visits are guided by Les Amis de Vauquois and need a reservation.
new.q: Butte de Vauquois, Vauquois

new.title: Swim and sail at Lac de Madine
new.desc: Two supervised beaches at Nonsard and Heudicourt open in July and August, and the water is rated excellent. A sailing centre rents sailboats, windsurfers, canoes and paddles.
new.tip: Swimming is free in the marked zones. A voie verte circles the lake.
new.q: Lac de Madine, Nonsard-Lamarche

new.title: Cycle EuroVelo 19 along the Meuse from Verdun
new.desc: The Verdun to Dun-sur-Meuse stage is about 42 km along the river, with 19 km on a dedicated path. The route continues south to Saint-Mihiel.
new.tip: Check bridge works near Verdun before setting out. Bikes travel free on the trains.
new.q: Quai de la République, Verdun

new.title: Spend a day at Amnéville Zoo and the thermal resort
new.desc: The zoo shows about 1,500 to 2,000 animals of 360 species on 18 hectares. Nearby are the Thermapolis spa, an aquarium and leisure attractions.
new.tip: Plan a full day. Check season opening hours.
new.q: Zoo d'Amnéville, Amnéville

new.title: Join the medieval festival at Rodemack
new.desc: Rodemack Cité Médiévale en Fête is the largest medieval festival in Moselle, held on the last weekend of June. The 2026 edition was the 46th.
new.tip: Dress up and arrive early to park.
new.q: Rodemack, Moselle

new.title: Attend the medieval festival at Sierck castle
new.desc: The Fête du Château de Sierck-les-Bains takes place each August in the castle of the dukes of Lorraine. The 2026 edition was listed for 22 and 23 August.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes for the stairs.
new.q: Château des ducs de Lorraine, Sierck-les-Bains

new.title: Visit the RenaissanceS festival in Bar-le-Duc
new.desc: The Festival RenaissanceS fills the Renaissance Ville Haute each year, usually on the first weekend of July.
new.tip: Check the programme for dates. Wear flat shoes for the cobbles.
new.q: Ville Haute, Bar-le-Duc

new.title: Walk the Vallée des Éclusiers by the inclined plane
new.desc: Walking routes start from the car park of the Saint-Louis-Arzviller inclined plane and follow the canal valley, popular with walkers and cyclists.
new.tip: Combine it with a boat trip on the lift.
new.q: Parking P3 Plan incliné de Saint-Louis-Arzviller, Saint-Louis
